subject: geography

moments.title: Rostow's Stages of Economic Growth
moments.body: Rostow publishes 'The Stages of Economic Growth: A Non-Communist Manifesto'. Five stages: traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity, age of high mass consumption. Britain takes off c. 1783; the US 1840s; Russia 1890s; India 1950s.
moments.takeaway: Rostow was an anti-communist Cold Warrior; the book's subtitle is explicit. The model framed US development aid policy for a generation.

moments.title: Frank's dependency theory
moments.body: Frank's 'Capitalism and Underdevelopment in Latin America' (1967) attacks Rostow. Underdevelopment is not a starting condition but a result — peripheral countries are kept poor by extracting surplus to the core. The metropolis-satellite framework derives from Marxist theory and Latin American structuralism (Prebisch).
moments.takeaway: Dependency theory dominated development economics in the 1970s. It informed import-substitution industrialisation across Latin America.

moments.title: Sen's capabilities
moments.who: Amartya Sen, Indian economist, Nobel laureate 1998
moments.body: Sen's 'Development as Freedom' (1999) reframes development from income growth to expansion of capabilities — what people can actually do and be. The Human Development Index (UNDP, with Mahbub ul Haq, from 1990) operationalises the approach.
moments.takeaway: The HDI combines life expectancy, education and income. Sen's framework underpins much modern development policy.

now.title: Development now
now.body: China's rise (since 1978) and India's (since 1991) reshaped the debate. East Asian 'developmental states' (Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam) fit neither pure Rostow nor pure dependency. The SDGs (2015) explicitly integrate multiple dimensions: poverty, gender, environment, governance. Climate change adds urgent new constraints.
now.open_questions: Is there a single development model? No consensus. Recent work (Daron Acemoglu, James Robinson) emphasises institutions; others (Ha-Joon Chang) emphasise state-led catch-up; ecological economists emphasise biophysical limits.

reflection: Development theory has cycled through optimism about convergence (Rostow), pessimism about structural traps (Frank), and pluralism about ends (Sen). Each generation has reshaped the question as much as the answers.
